Onboarding Process

Michael is in charge of creating the tickets for new users. The ticket should appear in Atera as “User Change Request: XXXXX”. On Michael’s side, the types of responses change, so make sure that the proper procedure is followed. Double check to make sure that the user does require an account in AD, some new employees just need an email, which is done in Admin 365 only.
Michael created a form for creating tickets, you can access the original form this way:
From the Atera ticket, scroll down to Michael’s ticket and right-click on “View All Responses” and open in a new incognito window.
Sign in as csitech@calgarywinterclub.com to access the form.
Once logged in, IT New User Request should be visible – enter it, then in the upper-right corner, enter “View Responses”.
This should take you to a page that shows all responses, the latest response will most likely be the form Michael filled out as part of the ticket.

Determine if the user is created in Admin 365 or in Active Directory. If the user is created in AD always perform changes on AD even if the same options exist in Admin 365 (example: resetting passwords).
Create the new user in the proper folder (this can either be a general “Users” folder or a folder specifically for their department), DC113 or DC114 can both be used.
For CWC, the name format is
firstnamelastinitial@calgarywinterclub.com
John Doe → johnd@calgarywinterclub.com

If applicable, you can use a departing user as a template for the new user (ask the ticket creator beforehand). Add the user’s job title in “Description” if other users in the company have their job title listed as well.
When creating a user, make sure to use the @calgarywinterclub.com email, never .local unless stated otherwise. In “Attributes”, under proxyaddress, add the user’s new email address:
Example: SMTP:johnd@calgarywinterclub.com

Add the new user into the relevant share folders and security groups that the ticket creator did not add in the New User Request Form. Whenever pushing syncs in AD, open Powershell as admin and use the command Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta to push changes to 365. CWC does not have a DeltaSync file on its DC.
Make sure to use the Secret Sharing system from Club Support when sending passwords!
https://csms.clubsupportinc.com/secrets
Granting Licenses
Log in to Microsoft 365 with the csitech@calgarywinterclub.com account.
https://admin.cloud.microsoft/?#/homepage

Find the newly created user and under Licenses, grant the license (if any) requested by the ticket creator, which should be outlined in the New User Request Form. If a license is required, send an email to “Licenses@clubsupportinc.com” under this format:

	Subject: Add (1/2/etc.) license to Calgary Winter Club

Body:

	License is for:

	User Requesting License (username@calgarywinterclub.com)
Exchange Online/Business Standard Monthly/Yearly Commit
Requested by
Michael Scullen		Ticket No.

Depending on the club, mailbox delegation, distribution lists, and other 365-exclusive groups should also be assigned in Exchange. To do so, go to “Exchange”, then depending on the mailbox, grant the proper permissions. For example, if you want to delegate the shared mailbox “Catering” to the user, go to the catering mailbox, and add the new user under the “Read and Manage” permissions.

Outlook usually adds the inbox to the user’s mailbox automatically, but if this doesn’t occur, you can add the mailbox manually in Outlook. To do this, right-click the account name in the left folder pane, select Add shared folder or mailbox, enter the mailbox address.

tabs.tab: Proper Server Shutdown and Startup Procedure

blocks.text: Consult with Yurii/Stan, Michael, and possibly any managers before doing any server shutdowns and startups. They are in charge of the regularly scheduled server reboots for most of the clubs, including CWC. If they are unavailable, contact Kosta as we do not reboot servers without prior consent.
Offboarding Process - Active Directory
Club Support Policy dictates that we rarely, if ever delete accounts in systems once created. Permissions and security group memberships in AD are generally left intact.

Reset the password to ensure that the user cannot sign-in with their previous credentials. Afterwards, right click the user to be offboarded, and press “Disable” if requested. If any changes are done, make sure to run the DeltaSync command on Powershell:
Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delt
Offboarding Process - Microsoft 365

The offboarding process differs from club to club, so double check the ticket as the creator will usually include what needs to be taken off and what needs to be retained. Depending on the outgoing user’s department, they might require a license to redirect emails properly.

Log in to the 365 portal with csitech@calgarywinterclub.com and find the user to be offboarded. To disallow the user from signing back in, press both “Block Sign-in” and “Sign Out Of All Sessions” to remove the user.

To unlicense a user, go to “Licenses” and remove their Microsoft 365 Basic/Standard license to remove their Outlook and Word license. If the license isn’t immediately being transferred to another user, you can remove the license by emailing Licenses@clubsupportinc.com
Subject: Remove (1/2/etc.) license in Calgary Winter Club

Body:

In Exchange, go to the user to be offboarded, and convert their mailbox into a shared mailbox. If Read Access, Send, or Send As access is requested by the ticket creator, this is also done in Exchange. Email forwarding is also done in Exchange if requested by the ticket creator.

New PC / Laptop Setup Guide
STEP 1 – GATHER IMPORTANT INFORMATION
Before replacing the old PC/laptop, collect the following information
Required Information

items: Printer information (what printers they have access to)
CMD for: Hostname (existing PC name) and whoami (User login details)
Ask the user for their password

blocks.text: Backup Important User Data

Export bookmarks and saved passwords and save them temporarily to  Desktop, Documents, or OneDrive. Check if files are in Downloads as well and copy them to Desktop, Documents, and/or OneDrive as necessary. Desktop/Documents usually do not need manual backup but always verify before assuming data is server-synced.
Check Folder Redirection / Offline Files
Determine whether folders are available offline. If necessary, contact the office to configure offline files properly.
AFTER INFORMATION IS COLLECTED

Once all information and backups are complete, remove PC from the DC. This way AD stays clean or rename it if PC gets repurposed. Power off the old PC and install/power on the new PC. If replacing a laptop, it may be easier to leave the old one running temporarily for reference.
STEP 2 – ADD PC TO THE DOMAIN
Login
Login to the domain controller (C006DC113/C006DC114) under your CSI-NAME account. If you require the Csupport credentials, feel free to ask your immediate supervisor/manager.
Renaming the PC and Joining the Domain.

Go to This PC -> Properties -> Domain or Workgroup -> Change and enter the domain name. In this case, it is calgarywinterclub.local. This will require a restart and the server administrator credentials.
The naming convention for CWC is based on the device type, not the user or month/year of installation. To keep the naming consistent, follow this naming convention:
C006[WS/LT/POS][Number]
For example, the most recent device installed was a laptop, making the name (C006LT344). Check Atera and see what the highest number value is.
STEP 3 – ADD PRINTERS
Method 1 – From Server
Install printers directly from \\C006PS117
Method 2 – Windows Printer Settings
Navigate to Settings -> Printers and dd printers manually if necessary.
Some printers require manufacturer drivers, make sure to print test pages if unsure which printer is correct and to test connections.
STEP 4 – REMOTE DESKTOP / WORK FROM HOME
Enable RDP

While logged into the CSupport account on the new device, navigate to Remote Desktop settings and enable RDP access. Allow the user's account to remote into the PC and verify that RDP permissions are enabled for their account.
To create the shortcut, enter Remote Desktop Connection, input the device IP address (from CMD -> ipconfig) and save the RDP shortcut to the desktop.
VPN Setup
Currently CHG uses SonicWall as their VPN, so refer to the separate guide for the complete setup. Once that’s finished, test the VPN by:
Connecting laptop to a hotspot
Starting the VPN
Login with user credentials
If VPN setup fails, uninstall WAN Miniports in Device Manager, reboot the device, and retry.
STEP 5 – USER ACCOUNT CONFIGURATION
Taskbar Cleanup

Change the taskbar settings in Settings -> Personalization -> Taskbar Settings and adjust taskbar preferences, including changing the search icon, removing the weather/current news popup on the left, and aligning the icons to the left or center.
Make sure to remove the unnecessary icons such as 365 Copilot and pin the necessary ones, such as Chrome, Adobe, Word, etc.
Set Default Applications
Configure defaults such as Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.
Install Additional Applications

Install any non-standard applications required by the user. Some applications require admin rights. Adobe Creative Cloud should be installed under the CSupport account. Obtain the Northstar POS link (if required).
Microsoft Account Sign-In
Have the user sign into Microsoft services  and complete MFA setup if required. Make sure OneDrive is backing up the Desktop/Documents as redirected folders are no longer used.
Final Data Restore
Re-add printers if needed, restore Downloads folder contents, and import browser bookmarks/passwords into the preferred browser.
Install SentinelOne and TeamViewer

SentinelOne requires an installation package from K2, while Teamviewer can be installed thorugh the Club Support website. Go to the website, then Client Support, then scroll down to install TeamViewer. Make sure to set the password to the standard Club Support password!
Remove Bloat

Depending on the original model of the new workstation/laptop, there will be most likely be some bloatware left on the device. As the admin account, disable UAC and uninstall unnecessary programs that were left over during the installation.
Enable RDP

While logged into the CSupport account on the new device, navigate to Remote Desktop settings and enable RDP access. Allow the user's account to remote into the PC and verify that RDP permissions are enabled for their account.
To create the shortcut, enter Remote Desktop Connection, input the device IP address (from CMD -> ipconfig) and save the RDP shortcut to the desktop.
Winter Club users also need to be connected to the VPN before they are able to connect remotely. Access depends on the user and their role.
RDP Setup
Make sure you have/check
The user's office computer name/terminal server name or IP address (can be found in Atera)
VPN access  (for remote connection only)
Remote Desktop access enabled on the office computer and user has been added to the list of who can remotely access the PC (Check security groups!)
Sleep is disabled on the office computer
The user's username and password.
RDP Connection
Confirm the user is connected to the VPN
Verify the office or remote computer is online by pinging its computer name or IP address.
Open Remote Desktop Connection on the user’s home computer by pressing Windows Key + R, typing mstsc, and pressing Enter.
Enter the office computer name or terminal server name into Remote Desktop Connection.
Enter the user’s domain username and password when prompted.
Accept the security warning to continue connecting.
Once connected, verify the user can access their network drives, applications, cameras, and any other required resources.

Create a saved RDP shortcut by opening RDC, entering the server name and your username, clicking Show Options, choosing Save As, saving the .rdp file to your desktop, and later opening that file to launch the connection automatically.
FortigateClient is the VPN used by CWC. Michael has the relevant information, such as pre-shared key, server, etc. so we will need to obtain this from him before adding someone into the VPN.
VPN access is managed via AD through the Fortigate VPN Users group and Exchange - BYOD Agreement Signed security group in 365 as well.

Installing Printers on workstations
Find the name of the printer to be installed in the C106PS116 server.
Make sure that the user has the relevant group membership for the printer to be used (Administration, Fitness, etc.).
In File Explorer, put \\C106PS116 into the File Explorer and this should bring up a list of all printers that are available to the user account.
Find the printer to be installed and double-click it to automatically install the printer drivers.
Send a test print to the printer to verify it’s connectivity.

Phones

Winter Club phone system is managed by a third-party company, CommunicationsPlus. Send any inquiries to Michael, but also run them by Artem as if the solution is simple enough, it might be solvable by Club Support. Phones are a mix of modern VOIP phones and very outdated handsets from 1980s and it causes issues.
Cameras

Cameras are handled by Avigilion, and the software used is called ExactQVision. The installer is located in the Shared Drive and should be accessible by any domain-joined user. Users with camera access have their own credentials to access their relevant cameras, and this is given to the user by Michael.
Cable
All TVs in the Winter Club are provided by Shaw Communications. Send any inquiries to Michael, make sure all tickets are directed to Shaw as we have no control over their cable.
Wi-Fi Networks
There are three (technically four) networks used in the Club
Calgary Winter Club: Open for all
CWC-Members: Password-locked network exclusively for members

CWC-Corp: Locked network exclusively for corporate staff (in admin office, managers, etc.). Used to be based on Windows credentials in AD but it is currently password-locked like CWC-Members for the handful of people that can’t use it (Mac users etc.)
RogersOpen: Free network provided by Rogers, use as testing for VPN.
Server Room Locations
There are many server racks in the Calgary Winter Club that are used for connections. Here are all of the locations from the starting point of the front entrance (where you pick up the keys):

Head to the glass doors on the left, go down the hallway all the way until you see a set of stairs, then head to the right hallway (the one with the slight incline) until you see a stairway/wheelchair elevator. The 55+ room door should be there, enter it, and then enter the door closest to your left.
Server Room

Head to the glass doors on the left, go down the hallway all the way until you see a set of stairs. Head upstairs and once in the brown hallway, make an immediate left until you enter the Admin Office (glass doors). Once inside, make your way to the cubicles. Michael’s office is on the area closest to your right, the main server room is on the door on the wall.
Chem

Head to the glass doors on the left, go down the hallway all the way until you see a set of stairs, then head to the right hallway (the one with the slight incline) until you see an open area with a locker room. The Chem Room rack is in the end of the room.
Tennis Rack

Head to the glass doors on the left, go down the hallway all the way until you see a set of stairs, then head straight towards the curling area. Enter the narrow hallway and keep walking straight past the elevator until you reach a ramp/stairs area. The tennis rack is in the double doors to your left once entering the tennis area.
R&R
Head to the stairs on the right, go upstairs until you see the entrance to the R&R and Elevation room. The server is inside the coat rack, inside the double doors.
